stories.title: 4 guards of Sardar Khetran held after body recovered from Barkhan property
summary: QUETTA: Police said on Sunday they have detained four guards of former Balochistan minister Sardar Abdul Rehman Khetran following the reported recovery of a body from his property in Barkhan district.
On Nov 18, Barkhan police registered a case against Khetran; his two sons, Islam Shah and Abdul Rauf; and three other accomplices on charges of murder, kidnapping and illegal confinement.
Khan Muhammad Marri, a former guard of Khetran, had said the bodies were of his wife Granaz and two sons, alleging they were kept in private jails.

stories.title: Afghan tradition keeps grapes fresh for winter treat
summary: KALAKAN: On the outskirts of Afghanistan’s frenetic capital Kabul, Muhammad Saber Shojaei is carrying out a centuries-old task of preserving fistfuls of grapes to be eaten when winter bites.

Carefully putting a bunch of grapes in one of the discs, Shojaei added a second disc on top and sealed the disc with mud before placing it in a dark storage room. “In this way, Kanginas can keep grapes fresh from now until the spring,” said the farmer.
But in the depths of winter, Afghans living near the vineyards can buy them along the roadside or in nearby markets, and farming families can crack them open and enjoy fresh grapes.

stories.title: Presidential ordinance withdraws most privileges of KP MPAs, including protection against preventive detention
summary: Two of the ordinances envisage setting up an executive committee with wide-ranging powers to oversee special initiatives, including developmental schemes, in the 12 designated districts and the rest of the province, respectively.
The committee will have powers to identify and recommend the executing agency for special initiatives in the designated and other districts, including military formations.

Both the ordinances provide for the establishment of an executive committee comprising a chairman, vice chairman and other such members as nominated by the prime minister, in case of designated district, and by the governor of the province, in case of the remaining districts.

stories.title: Internet provider expects submarine cable repairs to be completed by Dec 6
summary: Internet service provider Transworld Associates has said repair work on an affected international submarine cable is expected to be completed by December 6, with users likely to experience slower internet speeds during peak hours until the work is finished.

The development follows an earlier announcement by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) that a fault had been reported in the SEA-ME-WE 5 (SMW5) international submarine cable system, approximately 11 kilometres from Pakistan’s coast.
Internet monitoring organisation NetBlocks had also reported a decline in connectivity in Pakistan, saying the incident was consistent with a fault in the SMW5 international subsea cable system.

stories.title: At SCO moot in India, Musadik Malik declares climate change ‘enemy’ of civilisations
summary: Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik on Saturday declared climate change an “enemy” of civilisations as he highlighted its impact on South Asian countries at a meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in India.

We’re here to celebrate these things today.” Meetings with Indian minister, others Dr Malik arrived at Purana Qila in New Delhi for the second day of the inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, according to a post shared by his office earlier in the day.

In his meeting with Tajikistan’s Minister of Culture Sattoriyon Amonzoda, Malik underscored the strong historical and cultural ties between the two countries, the Pakistan High Commission in India said.

stories.title: Security forces kill 15 terrorists in Balochistan's Mastung district: state media
summary: Security forces have killed 15 terrorists during two separate operations in Balochistan’s Mastung district, state media reported on Saturday.
According to security sources cited by Radio Pakistan, five terrorists were killed in the first operation, while 10 others were eliminated in the second one.
Security forces remain committed to eradicating terrorism from Balochistan, and operations will continue until the last terrorist is eliminated, security sources asserted.

stories.title: CCD's school bag inspections in Punjab spark criticism on social media
summary: After the CCD set up a checking point outside a college in Lahore on Friday, it issued a press release on Saturday announcing a special campaign across educational institutions in Punjab to protect children from drugs, cigarettes, vapes and other intoxicating substances.

According to the press release by a CCD spokesperson, special checking desks have been established outside educational institutions, where students’ bags were searched to ensure that no intoxicating substances were taken inside, knowingly or unknowingly.

Former Punjab minister Arslan Khalid also questioned the presence of police personnel outside educational institutions, saying schools should not rely on police to discipline children. “Parents and teachers are enough to teach discipline to the children.

stories.title: Govt expenses squeeze development
summary: The ever-expanding administrative machinery of Pakistan is putting additional pressure on public finances at a time when the country needs to generate millions of jobs, attract private investment and accelerate development spending.

The report suggests that expanding administrative establishments without clearly defining responsibilities and financing arrangements could further increase government expenditure without necessarily improving public service delivery.

For Pakistan, where fiscal constraints continue to limit development spending and millions of new workers are entering the labour market, the effectiveness of government institutions is becoming an increasingly important part of the economic reform agenda.

stories.title: EU proposes 40b Euros cut to long-term budget
summary: The chairman of European Union leaders proposed further cuts to the European Commission's draft EU 2028-2034 budget on Saturday and suggested new revenue streams for the EU, including a digital tax, to help finance EU policies.
Costa's proposal mainly cuts the European Competitiveness Fund - aimed at helping make European industry more competitive against China and the United States - defence and external spending.

Friedrich Merz, the chancellor of Germany, which is the biggest net contributor to the budget and has repeatedly called for the budget to be slashed by hundreds of billions of euros, said the proposal was a first step, but still too high.

stories.title: Easing oil prices fail to lift PSX
summary: AHL Research stated that the KSE-100 closed at 177,383 points, down 0.28% week-on-week (WoW), as mild profit-taking after recent gains offset support from easing oil prices and post-US midterm optimism.
AHL mentioned that technology exports rose 17% YoY and 4% MoM to $453 million in Oct'26, making up 47% of total services exports.

Mohsin Shafi Qureshi of JS Global noted that the KSE-100 index edged down 491 points (0.3% WoW) to close at 177,383, amid political noise over a referendum on new provinces, with softer international oil prices offering limited support.

stories.title: Minister calls for secure data sharing among institutions
summary: Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal has called for strengthening data-sharing mechanisms among government institutions to promote evidence-based policymaking, improve coordination and ensure effective utilisation of official statistics.

Chairing a meeting at the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) headquarters, he stressed the need for a secure mechanism for sharing data between PBS, federal ministries and public sector organisations.

Secretary Planning Dr Muhammad Tahir Noor said effective utilisation of PBS data was essential for informed policymaking, and he stressed the need for efficient data sharing with line ministries, provincial governments and other stakeholders.

stories.title: PTA conducts live network tests in Multan
summary: Headed by Amir Shahzad, Director General (Enforcement), the PTA team met Member of National Assembly Ali Qasim Gillani, who appreciated the launch of 5G services in Multan and said it had contributed to improving telecom service quality in the city.
The PTA team assured him that its zonal office focal person would work with telecom operators and the Universal Service Fund (USF) to address these gaps and identify the need for additional sites.
Earlier, the PTA team met cellular and fixed-line operators, cable operators and telecom industry representatives in Multan.

stories.title: Export financing risks failure
summary: The challenge, he says, is not simply to make financing cheaper or relax eligibility conditions, but to create productive businesses capable of winning repeat orders, improving export prices and sustaining their presence in international markets.

Businesses that most need long-term financing are often those with export shares of 20% or 30%, which are trying to move into international markets rather than companies already deriving almost all their revenue from exports.
This would reveal whether the relaxed eligibility conditions are actually bringing new businesses into export markets or primarily benefiting existing exporters.

stories.title: India's Congress warns of more protests against Meta after clashes with police outside its offices
summary: The youth wing of India’s main opposition Congress party on Saturday warned of more protests against Meta’s removal of some accounts and posts of its members, a day after clashing with police outside the US firm’s India offices.
Congress has long accused Meta and other social media platforms of curbing dissent online by removing party accounts, favouring Modi’s government.

On Saturday, the Congress wing posted a video of its workers putting up a banner in central Delhi taking a dig at Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, referring to him as “Mark BJPberg” to allege the company’s favouritism towards Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party.

stories.title: Capt Safdar seeks Rs10bn in damages from Advocate Mian Dawood over 'defamatory' remarks
summary: According to the notice, the dispute arose from Safdar’s public demand that former president of the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA), Ahsan Bhoon, produce his LLB degree, a matter it says is already before the Supreme Court and the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC).
The notice claimed that Safdar had said he would apologise if Bhoon’s degree proved genuine and that Advocate Dawood, an “unrelated third party”, responded with malice.
The Punjab Defamation Tribunal had admitted the suit for hearing and issued a notice to Safdar.

stories.title: China renews UNSC push to sanction BLA, Majeed Brigade
summary: China on Thursday renewed its call at the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) to place the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and its suicide wing, the Majeed Brigade, on the UNSC’s 1267 sanctions list.
China has renewed its call at the UN to place the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and its Majeed Brigade on the UNSC’s 1267 sanctions list.

The latest statement from Beijing follows previous attempts by China to persuade the UNSC Sanctions Committee to list the BLA and Majeed Brigade in the past, but certain members blocked the move, citing a lack of enough evidence against the terrorist outfit.

stories.title: Interior minister meets JI chief in Lahore, discusses country's 'overall situation'
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Saturday met with Jamaat-i-Islami chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman in Lahore, where both discussed the “overall situation” in the country as well as challenges facing the public.
In a statement, the interior ministry said Naqvi and Rehman also exchanged views on law and order measures during the “important” meeting.
According to a press release issued by JI, Rehman said the government should also take measures to improve law and order.

stories.title: US court hands Indian national Nikhil Gupta 20 years for Sikh murder plot
summary: According to the DOJ, Gupta worked with Vikash Yadav, a co-defendant and Indian government employee, to organise the 2023 assassination.
Gupta allegedly passed this information to the undercover operative and kept Yadav informed about the progress of the operation.
The case has also been linked to the June 2023 killing of Sikh nationalist leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada, though Gupta’s defence denied his involvement in Nijjar’s assassination.

stories.title: Rizwan, Shan, Saim among notable omissions as PCB awards contracts to 38 players
summary: Players on Test-only contracts, however, would be encouraged to prioritise four-day cricket if taking up additional playing commitments.
Existing incentives include doubled match fees for victories against higher-ranked opponents and half the Test match fee for contracted players appearing in domestic four-day cricket.
Players awarded central contracts Test and ODI: Babar Azam, Salman Ali Agha.

stories.title: Democrats won big in the US midterms. Now what?
summary: Democrats basking in their Nov 3 election wins will soon unveil an ambitious legislative agenda for the first 100 days and beyond, in a test of progressives’ influence and Republicans’ willingness to cooperate, as they take control of the US Congress on Jan 3.
Aggressive agenda For months, Democrats have been plotting a House-Senate coordinated attack to undo Trump’s major accomplishments, according to ⁠lawmakers and aides.
Meanwhile, moderate Democrats, who outnumber progressives in Congress, have largely shied away from the universal healthcare “Medicare for All” idea progressives demand.

stories.title: President Zardari meets FM Dar, NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq to discuss 'overall political situation'
summary: President Asif Ali Zardari met Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq on Saturday to discuss political affairs amid the ongoing controversy over the subject of new provinces and a referendum.
Read: PTI backs referendum on new provinces Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi claimed on July 31 that the existing political system needed a reset with the creation of new provinces.

The interior minister, who is regarded as close to the powers that be, however, reiterated his stance on several occasions after the Sindh Assembly passed the resolution, which is dominated by the PPP, the second most important party in the current political dispensation.

stories.title: After nearly three-month delay, police submit charge sheet in Hina Javed murder case
summary: RAWALPINDI: After a delay of nearly three months, police have completed their investigation into the murder of Hina Javed and submitted the charge sheet to the court, Rawalpindi City Police Officer Sardar Ghias Gul told the media on Saturday.
Her husband and their domestic worker were arrested as Hina’s family accused them of murdering her, while her father-in-law was questioned as part of the investigation.
The police arrested Hina’s husband and their domestic servant, Zeeshan, in connection with the murder.

stories.title: Mexico captures top drug lord 'El Chapo Isidro,' latest in string of arrests
summary: The capture, the country's defence ministry said in a ​post on X, was carried out by special forces from Mexico's army and National Guard and done ‌with ⁠coordination between US and Mexican intelligence agencies.
The post said that cartel roadblocks had been set up in nearby municipalities, but that security forces were deployed alongside local authorities to clear them.

Social media videos from Guasave, Sinaloa, where Chapo Isidro was captured on Friday ​night, showed Mexican security ​force helicopters firing ⁠at ground targets, residents scrambling to seek cover at a baseball game and others hiding for safety by a night market.

stories.title: Iranian army claims it targeted US F-16 jet with missile over Gulf
summary: Iran's army said on Saturday that a US F-16 fighter jet was damaged when an Iranian air defence missile exploded near the aircraft over the Gulf on Friday evening, forcing the pilot to abort the mission and make an emergency landing.

The army's public relations office said domestically developed air defence systems deployed in southern Iran detected and identified the fighter jet while operating under the country's integrated air defence network, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported.
This is FALSE. ✅ FACT: Iran did not attack a U.S. F-16 fighter aircraft yesterday — at all.

stories.title: FM Dar calls for multilateralism, says bloc or unilateral politics will not work
summary: On mediation efforts between the US and Iran, FM Dar said Pakistan was the first country to condemn Israel’s attack on Iran on February 28.
The foreign minister said that even during the previous round of indirect talks between the US and Iran in Oman, it had been agreed that Pakistan must be present if direct talks were held.
Dar said New Delhi had wrongly blamed Islamabad for the Pahalgam attack as a pretext for the May 2025 conflict between Pakistan and India.

stories.title: 15 terrorists killed in security operations in Balochistan’s Mastung district: state media
summary: Security forces killed 15 terrorists in two separate major operations in Balochistan’s Mastung district as part of the ongoing Operation Radd-ul-Fitna-3 against Fitna al-Hindustan, state media outlet Radio Pakistan reported on Saturday.
Radio Pakistan further stated that security forces remained committed to eliminating terrorism from Balochistan, with operations set to continue until the last terrorist was eliminated.
On November 13, security forces killed 74 terrorists during operations in Balochistan and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.

stories.title: COP31 climate summit risks failure as talks go deep into overtime
summary: The COP31 climate summit will either produce a good deal or no ​deal at all, the European Union's top climate official said on Saturday as talks stretched deep into overtime.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries ‌are struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance, delaying an agreement at the two-week conference that had been scheduled to end on Friday.

Asked about the chances of no deal emerging, he said: "We will ​find out." The last major breakdown in UN climate talks came in Copenhagen in 2009, when countries failed to adopt the Copenhagen ​Accord by consensus in a setback for multilateral climate diplomacy.

stories.title: SICVD treats 22,639 heart attack patients, performs 1,626 surgeries in 10 months
summary: The Sindh Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (SICVD) treated 22,639 heart attack patients through angiography and angioplasty and performed 1,626 open-heart surgeries between January and October 2026, according to a statement issued by the institute.

During the 10-month period, the institute’s network of 30 chest pain units across Sindh handled 463,975 emergency cases, while its triage and emergency departments received a total of 598,401 patients, the statement said.
The institute’s catheterisation laboratories also performed diagnostic angiography on 7,210 patients, who were subsequently referred for medical management or surgery.

stories.title: FBI's criminal information database hacked, CNN reports
summary: The FBI is investigating a suspected breach of a nationwide database ​used by federal, state and local ‌law enforcement agencies to share criminal justice information, CNN reported on Friday, citing two people briefed ​on the investigation.

The apparent compromise of the ​National Crime Information Centre database would ⁠mark the second intrusion involving an FBI ​system in recent months and the latest in ​a string of cyber incidents that have alarmed US officials over the past week.

Read: FBI and US Secret Service working with Binance after $6.3 billion hack, source says The FBI database is used by law enforcement ‌agencies ⁠nationwide to store and share information on warrants, criminal histories and background checks.

stories.title: States agree to UN talks aiming to regulate 'killer robots' by 2028
summary: UN talks on regulating weapons with little or no human oversight ended on Saturday with a pledge for further discussions to develop new rules within two years, an outcome weakened by Russia's opposition and disappointing human ​rights groups.

Proponents had called for legally binding rules within a short timeframe to regulate weapons ​systems that can identify and engage targets with varying degrees of autonomy, ⁠sometimes called "killer robots".
"Delaying the creation of a legally binding instrument puts civilians and humanity at risk,” said Nicole van Rooijen, executive director at Stop Killer Robots, on the sidelines of ⁠the talks.

stories.title: Parliamentary affairs minister invites PTI to join NA electoral reforms committee
summary: The government on Saturday invited the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) to join the National Assembly (NA) Electoral Reforms Committee (ERC), offering representation in proportion to the party’s strength in the lower house while rejecting its demand for equal representation.
The NA on October 16 passed a motion moved by Dr Chaudhry under Rule 244B to form a parliamentary committee comprising members from both houses to recommend electoral reforms.
The motion stipulated that parliamentary parties would be represented in proportion to their strength in Parliament.

stories.title: EU proposes tax on Big Tech to boost budget
summary: The EU put forward plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to fund its next budget Saturday, as it seeks to bridge divisions among member states over the bloc's long-term funding.

European Council President Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by 204 billion euros ($224 billion) a plan initially put forward by the European Commission, which some countries had slammed as too onerous.

Among these could be a tax on digital firms, which the draft Costa presented Saturday says will concern companies with an annual turnover for digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU as well as a global turnover of more than 750 million euros.

stories.title: From screens in class to smart glasses, Norway rethinks new technologies
summary: After making laptops and screens ubiquitous in schools across the country, Norway is bringing back textbooks in a bid to reverse a sharp decline in pupils' reading and writing skills.

"There is reason to believe that the introduction of screens in schools happened too quickly, before we had sufficient knowledge about their effects and about what constitutes good pedagogical use of digital devices," Norway's Digitalisation Minister Torgeir Micaelsen told AFP.
'Quick fixes' Norwegian authorities have, in turn, recommended regulating the use of mobile phones in schools and introducing artificial intelligence into the school curriculum only gradually.

stories.title: Videos, photos of 13-year-old domestic worker's torture at senior FIA official’s Islamabad residence emerge
summary: Read: Court extends remand of two suspects in Fatima murder case Earlier, a post-mortem report prepared by the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) revealed extensive injuries and signs of prolonged and brutal torture inflicted on the child.

Read: Court extends remand of two suspects in Fatima murder case Fatima was working as a domestic helper at the residence, which police identified as the official accommodation of a senior FIA officer located within the Islamabad Police Lines Headquarters.
The death of 13-year-old Fatima Asghar has once again drawn attention to the exploitation and abuse of children employed as domestic workers in Pakistan.

stories.title: FBI, US Agriculture Department breached by hackers: reports
summary: The US Agriculture Department and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) were breached by hackers in cyberattacks, US media reported on Saturday, as concerns deepened over the recent spate of tech outages at key American institutions.
The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) told employees that a system used to facilitate payments to farmers was targeted in a cyberattack, NBC reported on Friday, citing two former USDA officials.
The former official expressed concerns that hackers “could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on.” AFP has contacted the FBI and USDA for comment.

stories.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower on AI selloff, S&P 500, Dow in correction
summary: US stocks extended their rout on Friday, and the S&P ​500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections after Anthropic’s momentous debut fell flat, exacerbating worries about the AI trade that has driven this year’s stock market rally.

Anthropic’s supersized debut as a publicly held company, which was intended to raise as much as $2 trillion in market cap, failed to catch ​fire on Thursday, closing 17.1pc above its $83 offer price as enthusiasm for the stock faded throughout the session.
In its second day as a publicly held company, Anthropic’s shares fell 9.1pc; Nvidia’s shares tumbled 13.8pc.

stories.title: NIH issues nationwide advisories on flu, smog and vaccine-preventable diseases
summary: The advisories, issued by the NIH’s Centre for Disease Control, cover the prevention and control of seasonal influenza for 2026-27, health risks and precautionary measures associated with smog, as well as vaccine-preventable disease control.
Health authorities have further been directed to strengthen public awareness and risk communication to promote preventive measures against seasonal infections and smog-related health complications.
The NIH has urged all relevant health authorities and stakeholders across the country to implement the recommended measures promptly to minimise winter-related health risks and protect public health.

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition’s 'special operation'
summary: Yemen’s Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday, after vowing reprisals for a “special operation” by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them.

Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen’s civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition’s attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on Friday.

stories.title: Nearly 1,500 people stranded in Japan's Fukushima Prefecture due to heavy snow
summary: Nearly 1,500 people were stranded in a village in Japan's Fukushima Prefecture after heavy snow toppled trees and blocked roads, local authorities said on Saturday.

Those stranded include approximately 900 residents and 500 people staying at hotels and other accommodations in and around the Urabandai area of Kitashiobara village, Kyodo News Agency reported, citing authorities.
No injuries have been reported so far, according to authorities.

stories.title: As Trump basks in summit pomp, China's Xi strengthens his hand
summary: US President Donald Trump hailed the fanfare of his meeting this week with Xi Jinping as a victory, but the US president has gained little from three such summits this year while the Chinese ​leader has strengthened his position on the world stage, analysts say.

Xi emerged from a global gathering in China as a statesman who could convene the first China-US-Russia summit and he keeps a ‌fragile trade truce with the US in a holding pattern — where Beijing likes it — even as Washington takes a harder line.

"It may ​feel like a holding pattern by comparison to past summits, but in the current context it's actually a significant step, given the recent midterm elections and the Jensen Huang scandal." Analysts expect the year's fourth Trump-Xi meeting will also be heavy on optics.
